definitionEn: the period following a disaster, war or crisis, and the effects it leaves
situation: Describing the difficult period that follows a war, disaster or scandal, when people deal with the damage.

examples.text: Thousands of volunteers helped to clear the streets in the [[aftermath]] of the hurricane.
We spent Sunday morning cleaning up the [[aftermath]] of Saturday's birthday party.
The novel follows three families through the chaotic [[aftermath]] of the revolution, when food and work were scarce.

texts: Food prices rose sharply in the [[aftermath]] of the drought.
Counsellors visited the school to support pupils in the [[aftermath]] of the fire.
The coach refused to speak to reporters in the immediate [[aftermath]] of the defeat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Aftermath — всегда о тяжёлом периоде после беды. О хороших результатах говорят positive effects или benefits.

collocationTask.explanationRu: In the aftermath of — «после бедствия, когда разбираются с его последствиями». Result, outcome и effect в такой рамке не используют: говорят as a result of.

nuance.text: Many shops stayed closed for weeks in the [[aftermath]] of the floods.
nuance.explanationRu: Aftermath — период после беды и обстановка в это время. Consequence — отдельное последствие; оборота in the consequence of нет, говорят as a consequence of.

reverse.text: Higher bus fares are a direct [[consequence]] of the new fuel tax.
reverse.explanationRu: Конкретный результат решения — a consequence. Aftermath — не отдельное следствие, а тяжёлый период после события.

fixIt.text: Hundreds of families were left homeless in the [[result]] of the flood.
fixIt.explanationRu: In the result of — калька с «в результате». О периоде после бедствия говорят in the aftermath of, а о причине — as a result of.

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "How's the office after last week's big move?"
options: Brilliant! The aftermath was a lovely surprise party for the whole team.
Still a bit chaotic. We're dealing with the aftermath: boxes everywhere and no Wi-Fi yet.
The aftermath of the relocation is hereby being processed by the relevant personnel.
reply.explanationRu: Aftermath — неприятные последствия события, к празднику это слово не подходит. Третий вариант звучит как казённый отчёт, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: The town struggled for years after the factory closed down.
rewrite.frame: The town struggled for years in ____ of the factory closure.
rewrite.explanationRu: In the aftermath of — «после тяжёлого события и в его последствиях».

definitionEn: angry, hostile behaviour or feelings that may lead to attacking others
situation: Describing hostile, threatening behaviour in people or animals, such as shouting, pushing or trying to attack.

examples.text: Male deer show more [[aggression]] in the mating season, so photographers keep their distance.
The manager's constant [[aggression]] in meetings made junior staff afraid to share ideas.
Researchers tested whether violent video games make teenagers more prone to [[aggression]].

texts: Shouting at children can teach them [[aggression]] instead of respect.
Boxing helps him channel his [[aggression]] into something useful.
The treaty was meant to prevent further [[aggression]] between the two states.

badCollocation.noteRu: О своём настроении так не говорят. Скажите I feel angry или I'm really irritable today.

collocationTask.explanationRu: An act of aggression — устойчивое сочетание: враждебный, агрессивный шаг. Attack и fight уже сами обозначают действие, поэтому act of с ними не говорят.

nuance.text: Her emails were polite, but you could sense the hidden [[aggression]] in every line.
nuance.explanationRu: Aggression — враждебный настрой, который может звучать и в словах, и в тоне. Violence — физическое насилие, в вежливом письме его быть не может.

reverse.text: The film is not suitable for children because of its graphic [[violence]].
reverse.explanationRu: Сцены насилия в кино — graphic violence. Aggression — враждебное поведение или настрой, а не показанное на экране насилие.

fixIt.text: Some dogs show [[violence]] towards strangers when they feel threatened.
fixIt.explanationRu: О враждебном поведении животных говорят show aggression. Violence — физическое насилие, show violence в этом смысле не говорят.

wordFormation.text: Witnesses disagreed about which driver had been the [[aggressor]] in the roadside argument.

reply.context: A friend tells you: "My neighbour's dog growls and shows its teeth every time I walk past."
options: How sweet! It must feel a lot of aggression for you already.
One is advised to report such canine aggression to the relevant authority forthwith.
That sounds like real aggression. Maybe mention it to the owner before someone gets bitten.
reply.explanationRu: Aggression — враждебность, а не нежность, поэтому первый ответ не подходит. Второй звучит как официальное предписание, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: pleasant and enjoyable, or friendly and easy to like
senseNote: Здесь — «приятный»; значение «согласный на что-то» (if you are agreeable) встречается реже.
situation: Describing a pleasant evening, place or person that is easy to enjoy and causes no trouble.

examples.text: We spent a truly [[agreeable]] evening on the terrace, chatting, laughing and watching the sunset.
My new flatmate is very [[agreeable]]: easy-going, tidy and always ready to help.
The climate on the coast is [[agreeable]] all year, never too hot or too cold.

texts: The weather stayed [[agreeable]] for the whole of our holiday.
She found her new colleagues [[agreeable]] and easy to work with.
The soup had a rich, [[agreeable]] flavour of roasted peppers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Я с вами согласен» — I agree with you. Agreeable значит «приятный», и I'm agreeable with you звучит странно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Agreeable описывает и людей, и события: an agreeable surprise. Amiable, affable и obliging говорят только о людях — о приветливом и услужливом характере.

nuance.text: The spa has a calm, [[agreeable]] atmosphere and a lovely view of the lake.
nuance.explanationRu: Agreeable описывает и людей, и обстановку, погоду, вкус. Likeable — только о людях или героях, которые вызывают симпатию; likeable atmosphere не говорят.

fixIt.text: The hotel stood on a quiet, [[sympathetic]] square full of cafés and flower stalls.
fixIt.explanationRu: Sympathetic — «сочувствующий», а не «симпатичный». Приятное, уютное место описывают словом agreeable.

wordFormation.text: Despite the rain, the walk along the cliffs turned out to be surprisingly [[agreeable]].

definitionEn: connected with farming, growing crops or raising animals
situation: Describing land, machinery, jobs or policies that have to do with growing crops and keeping animals.

examples.text: Much of the forest was cleared to create new [[agricultural]] land for cattle and soya.
The region's economy is mainly [[agricultural]], with most families growing olives or grapes.
Students of [[agricultural]] science learn how soil, water and weather affect crops.

texts: Heavy rain destroyed large areas of [[agricultural]] land this spring.
Tractors and other [[agricultural]] machinery are expensive to repair.
The country exports mostly [[agricultural]] products such as wheat and sugar.

badCollocation.noteRu: Agricultural — прилагательное. «Работать в сельском хозяйстве» — work in agriculture или work on a farm.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Техника для полей — agricultural machinery. Rural, country и village описывают сельскую местность и жизнь, а не технику.

nuance.text: Rising fuel prices have hit [[agricultural]] exports such as grain and sunflower oil.
nuance.explanationRu: Agricultural — связанный с сельским хозяйством: продукция, техника, земля. Rural — связанный с сельской местностью (rural areas, rural life); rural exports не говорят.

reverse.text: Buses in [[rural]] Scotland can run as rarely as twice a day.
reverse.explanationRu: Rural Scotland — сельская глубинка Шотландии. Agricultural относится к фермерству, а не к местности.

fixIt.text: The factory produces tractors and other [[rural]] machinery for export.
fixIt.explanationRu: Rural — «сельский» о местности и жизни. Техника для полей — agricultural machinery.

wordFormation.text: Nearly half of the country's [[agricultural]] output comes from small family farms.

definitionEn: a person who assists a senior official or politician in their work
situation: Talking about the assistants who work closely with a president, minister or other senior official.

examples.text: The president arrived with two [[aides]] who carried his papers and managed his schedule.
A former [[aide]] has written a revealing book about life inside the mayor's office.
Her grandmother has a home-care [[aide]] who visits every morning to help her wash and dress.

texts: The senator's [[aides]] worked through the night to finish the speech.
Two presidential [[aides]] were questioned about the missing documents.
Nursing [[aides]] help patients eat, wash and move around the ward.

badCollocation.noteRu: Aide — человек-помощник. Помощь как ресурс — aid: humanitarian aid, first aid.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Помощника политика называют aide. Aid — это помощь, а не человек; helper и worker звучат слишком просто для такой должности.

nuance.text: A former [[aide]] to the governor has agreed to give evidence in court.
nuance.explanationRu: Aide — человек, помощник чиновника или политика. Aid — помощь (деньги, еда, лекарства), человеком быть не может.

reverse.text: The charity sends medical [[aid]] to areas hit by floods.
reverse.explanationRu: Медицинская или гуманитарная помощь — aid. Aide — человек-помощник, а не ресурс.

fixIt.text: A senior [[helper]] to the mayor was dismissed for leaking confidential documents.
fixIt.explanationRu: Helper — просто «тот, кто помогает». Помощник мэра или министра — aide.

definitionEn: used to add a fact that limits what was just said; although
situation: Adding a small contrast or limitation to a statement, usually in formal writing, before an adjective or short phrase.

examples.text: The project was a success, [[albeit]] a rather expensive one.
The economy is growing again, [[albeit]] more slowly than the government had hoped.
After a long discussion, my father agreed to lend us the car, [[albeit]] rather reluctantly.

texts: The hotel was comfortable, [[albeit]] a little far from the beach.
He apologised, [[albeit]] only after his manager insisted.
The band's new album is enjoyable, [[albeit]] less original than their first.

badCollocation.noteRu: После albeit обычно не ставят целое предложение с подлежащим: albeit slowly, albeit small. С полным предложением — although: although it was raining.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Albeit ставят перед наречием или короткой фразой: albeit briefly. После despite нужно существительное, а после whereas и because — целое предложение.

nuance.text: The team finished third, [[albeit]] with a much smaller budget than its rivals.
nuance.explanationRu: Albeit вводит уступку перед фразой: albeit with a smaller budget. Despite — предлог, после него сразу существительное (despite a smaller budget), с with он не сочетается.

reverse.text: The match went ahead [[despite]] the heavy rain.
reverse.explanationRu: Перед существительным нужен предлог despite. Albeit не работает как предлог: albeit the heavy rain — ошибка.

fixIt.text: The new policy is a step forward, [[despite]] a small one.
fixIt.explanationRu: Despite значит «несмотря на» и здесь бессмысленно. Чтобы добавить оговорку «хоть и небольшой», нужно albeit a small one.

reply.context: Your manager asks in a meeting: "So, did the new booking system work over the weekend?"
options: It did, albeit with a few delays on Saturday morning.
It did, albeit it crashed and we lost every single booking.
Albeit, like, it kinda worked, I guess?
reply.explanationRu: Albeit добавляет небольшую оговорку перед фразой. Во втором ответе «оговорка» перечёркивает весь смысл, а в третьем albeit стоит не к месту в небрежной разговорной фразе.

rewrite.original: Sales rose last month, although the rise was very small.
rewrite.explanationRu: Albeit + наречие: albeit slightly — «хоть и незначительно».

definitionEn: quick to notice things and ready to react, especially to danger
senseNote: Прилагательное «бдительный, собранный»; существительное alert (сигнал тревоги) здесь не тренируем.
situation: Describing someone who is wide awake, watching carefully and ready to notice danger or react quickly.

examples.text: Long-distance drivers should take regular breaks to stay [[alert]] at the wheel.
Although he is ninety, my grandfather is still mentally [[alert]] and does the crossword every day.
Staff have been told to remain [[alert]] to suspicious emails asking for passwords.

texts: A strong coffee keeps me [[alert]] during long afternoon meetings.
The guard dog was instantly [[alert]] when it heard footsteps.
Cyclists must stay [[alert]] to cars opening their doors.

badCollocation.noteRu: С alert используют предлог to: alert to the risks. Предлог of сюда по ошибке переносят из aware of.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Mentally alert — «с ясной головой, сообразительный». Careful, watchful и cautious описывают осторожное поведение, с mentally их не сочетают.

nuance.text: After three espressos, I felt wide awake and [[alert]].
nuance.explanationRu: Alert — «бодрый, собранный, всё замечающий». Careful — «осторожный, аккуратный» в действиях: кофе делает человека бодрым, а не осторожным.

reverse.text: Be [[careful]] with that pan — the handle is very hot.
reverse.explanationRu: Осторожно обращаться с чем-то — be careful with. Alert — про внимание и готовность заметить опасность, а не про аккуратность.

fixIt.text: After a sleepless night, I found it hard to stay [[careful]] during the afternoon meeting.
fixIt.explanationRu: Careful — «осторожный». Не клевать носом и сохранять ясную голову на встрече — stay alert.

wordFormation.text: Lack of sleep reduces your [[alertness]] more than you might think.

reply.context: Your flatmate says: "I've got a job interview at 8 a.m. tomorrow and I'm completely exhausted."
options: Great, being that tired will make you nice and alert for it.
Go to bed early, then. You'll want to be alert when they ask the tricky questions.
It is imperative that you maintain maximum alertness, my dear colleague.
reply.explanationRu: Alert — «собранный, с ясной головой», а усталость этому мешает, так что первый ответ нелогичен. Третий звучит как приказ начальника, а не совет соседу.

rewrite.original: Guards must watch carefully for anything unusual during the night shift.
rewrite.frame: Guards must stay ____ anything unusual during the night shift.
rewrite.explanationRu: Быть начеку, внимательно следить за чем-то — stay alert to.

definitionEn: strange, unfamiliar and not part of your normal experience or character
senseNote: Здесь — «чуждый, непривычный» (alien to someone), а не «инопланетный».
situation: Describing an idea, place or way of behaving that feels completely strange and unlike what you know.

examples.text: Having grown up in a tiny village, he found city life noisy, crowded and completely [[alien]].
Lying is so [[alien]] to her nature that she can't even keep a birthday surprise secret.
Many international students find British humour baffling and totally [[alien]] at first.

texts: Working from home felt [[alien]] to him after twenty years in an office.
Such rudeness is quite [[alien]] to the local culture.
Under the red sky, the desert landscape looked [[alien]] and hostile.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Чужой телефон» — someone else's phone. Alien значит «чуждый, непривычный», а не «принадлежащий другому».

collocationTask.prompt: Dishonesty was completely ___ to his nature.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Alien to someone's nature — «совершенно не свойственно». Odd, unknown и distant в сочетании to his nature в этом смысле не употребляют.

nuance.text: Such selfishness is [[alien]] to everything she believes in.
nuance.explanationRu: Alien to — «чуждо чему-то»: убеждениям, характеру, культуре. Strange в такой конструкции не работает: strange to everything she believes in звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: It's [[strange]] that nobody called to tell us about the delay.
reverse.explanationRu: «Странно, что» — it's strange that. Alien описывает что-то чуждое и непривычное, а не удивительный факт.

fixIt.text: The strict hierarchy at the bank felt completely [[alienated]] to me at first.
fixIt.explanationRu: Alienated описывает человека, который чувствует себя отчуждённым. Непривычные, чуждые правила — alien to me.

reply.context: A colleague who has just moved from Madrid to Oslo says: "People here eat dinner at five o'clock. Can you imagine?"
options: I can't! Eating that early would feel completely alien to me.
Wow, so Oslo must be full of alien people from Madrid now!
Indeed, such customs may be regarded as alien by persons of Iberian origin.
reply.explanationRu: Alien to me — «мне чуждо, непривычно». Во втором ответе alien ошибочно значит «приезжий», а третий звучит как научный отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: Being late for meetings is completely unlike his character.
rewrite.frame: Being late for meetings is completely ____ his nature.
rewrite.explanationRu: Alien to someone's nature — «совершенно не свойственно кому-то».

definitionEn: to make people feel unfriendly towards you or stop supporting you
situation: When someone's words or decisions make friends, customers or voters turn away from them.

examples.text: The company [[alienated]] loyal customers by suddenly doubling the subscription price.
The party risks [[alienating]] older voters if it cuts pensions.
Her habit of correcting everyone's grammar [[alienates]] even her closest friends.

texts: Aggressive pop-up ads can [[alienate]] visitors to your website.
Try not to [[alienate]] your colleagues during your first week.
The director didn't want to [[alienate]] fans of the original book.

badCollocation.noteRu: Alienate — переходный глагол: alienate someone. «Отдалиться от родителей» — grow apart from или drift away from your parents.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Настроить людей против себя — alienate. Distance употребляют как distance yourself from, reject — «отвергать», remove — «убирать».

nuance.text: Years of broken promises had slowly [[alienated]] the town's residents.
nuance.explanationRu: Alienate — постепенно оттолкнуть людей, лишиться их доверия и поддержки. Offend — задеть, обидеть в конкретный момент; «медленно обидеть» звучит странно.

reverse.text: I hope I didn't [[offend]] you with that joke about your accent.
reverse.explanationRu: Задеть человека одной шуткой — offend. Alienate — оттолкнуть, отдалить от себя, обычно постепенно или целую группу людей.

fixIt.text: The new manager's rudeness quickly [[distanced]] most of the team.
fixIt.explanationRu: Distance обычно употребляют как distance yourself from. Оттолкнуть людей своим поведением — alienate them.

wordFormation.text: Many teenagers go through a period of [[alienation]] from their parents and teachers.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Should we email our customers five special offers a week?"
options: I'd be careful. That many emails might alienate people rather than win them back.
Yes, five a week would alienate them in a good way: they'd feel really valued.
Such a frequency would inevitably precipitate the alienation of our esteemed clientele.
reply.explanationRu: Alienate — оттолкнуть, и «в хорошем смысле» оттолкнуть нельзя. Третий ответ звучит напыщенно и канцелярски для обычного обсуждения.

rewrite.original: The new rules made many long-time members turn against the club.
rewrite.frame: The new rules ____ many long-time members.
rewrite.explanationRu: Alienate someone — оттолкнуть, настроить против себя.

definitionEn: to adjust plans or ideas so that they match or support others
senseNote: Здесь — «приводить в соответствие, согласовывать», а не буквально «выравнивать в линию».
situation: Talking about making plans, goals or rules fit together or match something else, often at work.

examples.text: We need to [[align]] our marketing strategy with the company's new sustainability goals.
The new textbooks are [[aligned]] with the national curriculum, so teachers can use them immediately.
Before accepting the job, make sure the company's values [[align]] with your own.

texts: The central bank tried to [[align]] interest rates with those in neighbouring countries.
Couples need to [[align]] their expectations before planning a wedding.
Engineers must [[align]] the software update with the new hardware.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Согласовать встречу» — arrange или schedule a meeting. Align — приводить планы и цели в соответствие друг другу.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ your goals with the company's strategy
collocationTask.explanationRu: Привести цели в соответствие со стратегией — align them with it. Equal, level и straighten значат «равняться», «выравнивать поверхность», «выпрямлять».

nuance.text: Every project we fund must be [[aligned]] with our mission of reducing plastic waste.
nuance.explanationRu: Aligned with our mission — «соответствует миссии». Coordinate — организовать совместные действия людей или отделов; с миссией или ценностями его не сочетают.

reverse.text: A project manager [[coordinates]] the work of designers, writers and developers.
reverse.explanationRu: Организовать совместную работу людей — coordinate. Align — сверять цели и планы с чем-то, а не руководить работой.

fixIt.text: Our sales targets should be [[equalled]] with the company's long-term strategy.
fixIt.explanationRu: Equal — «равняться, сравняться» по величине. Привести цели в соответствие со стратегией — align them with it.

reply.context: Before a product launch, your boss asks the team: "Is there anything we still need to check?"
options: We should align the launch party with some balloons and loud music.
We should make sure the adverts align with our new brand guidelines.
Gotta align, like, all the stuff, innit?
reply.explanationRu: Align with — «соответствовать»: реклама должна соответствовать фирменному стилю. «Согласовать вечеринку с шарами» — бессмыслица, а третий ответ слишком небрежен для рабочей встречи.

rewrite.original: Our budget needs to match the goals we set for next year.
rewrite.frame: Our budget needs to ____ the goals we set for next year.
